comparisons.peer_topic: Factors affecting and methods for stock repurchases
comparisons.peer_summary: The timing and amount of common stock repurchases are subject to factors including capital position, liquidity, financial performance, regulatory requirements, and market conditions, and may be suspended at any time; repurchases may be effected through open market purchases or privately negotiated transactions, including Rule 10b5-1 plans.
comparisons.comparison: Both GS and BAC disclose that their share repurchase programs are governed by similar factors, specifically citing the firm's capital position and general market conditions as primary determinants of timing and amount. Both firms also utilize similar execution mechanisms, including open-market purchases and Rule 10b5-1 plans. A key difference is that BAC explicitly lists 'liquidity' and 'financial performance' as subject factors and notes repurchases may be 'privately negotiated', whereas GS emphasizes 'capital deployment opportunities' and 'prevailing price and trading volumes' alongside the Fed's quarterly plan approval process.

sentences.text: On an annual basis, we submit a Board of Directors of Group Inc. (Board) approved capital plan to the Federal Reserve, which includes planned share repurchases for each quarter.

The share repurchases are effected primarily through regular open-market purchases (which may include repurchase plans designed to comply with Rule 10b5-1 and accelerated share repurchases), the amounts and timing of which are determined primarily by our current and projected capital position, and capital deployment opportunities, but which may also be influenced by general market conditions and the prevailing price and trading volumes of our common stock.

The timing and amount of common stock repurchases are subject to various factors, including the Corporation's capital position, liquidity, financial performance and alternative uses of capital, stock trading price, regulatory requirements and general market conditions, and may be suspended at any time.

Such repurchases may be effected through open market purchases or privately negotiated transactions, including repurchase plans that satisfy the conditions of Rule 10b5-1 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (Exchange Act).

comparisons.peer_topic: Shareholder Returns and Capital Repurchase Program
comparisons.peer_summary: Citi returned $6.7 billion to shareholders in 2024 via dividends and repurchases, and authorized a new $20 billion multiyear repurchase program in January 2025 with $1.5 billion planned for Q1 2025, subject to regulatory capital uncertainty.
comparisons.comparison: While GS and C both discuss share repurchases within the context of capital management, their strategic contexts differ significantly regarding regulatory capital certainty. GS states it submits planned repurchases to the Federal Reserve annually as part of a standard capital plan, implying a routine process. In contrast, Citi explicitly states that its future repurchase assessments are conducted 'quarter-by-quarter given uncertainty regarding regulatory capital requirements,' highlighting a higher degree of regulatory caution not explicitly mentioned in GS's governance description for the same period.

sentences.text: On an annual basis, we submit a Board of Directors of Group Inc. (Board) approved capital plan to the Federal Reserve, which includes planned share repurchases for each quarter.

• Citi returned $6.7 billion to common shareholders in the form of dividends ($4.2 billion) and share repurchases ($2.5 billion) in 2024. As previously disclosed, on January 13, 2025, Citigroup's Board of Directors authorized a new, multiyear $20 billion common stock repurchase program, with planned repurchases of $1.5 billion during the first quarter of 2025, subject to market conditions and other factors. After the first quarter of 2025, Citi will continue to assess the level of common share repurchases on a quarter-by-quarter basis given uncertainty regarding regulatory capital requirements, among other factors.

comparisons.peer_topic: Common Share Repurchase Program Governance and Flexibility
comparisons.peer_summary: The Board's authorization allows management discretion to repurchase shares based on market conditions, capital position, and other factors, without specific price targets or timetables, and repurchases may be suspended at any time using various methods including Rule 10b5-1 plans.
comparisons.comparison: GS and JPM both emphasize the flexibility of their repurchase programs, noting that amounts and timing are determined by management based on capital position and market conditions rather than rigid constraints. Both disclosures mention the use of Rule 10b5-1 plans or open market purchases. A specific difference is that JPM explicitly states its authorization does not establish 'specific price targets or timetables' and allows for suspension at any time, whereas GS frames the constraints around the Federal Reserve's approved capital plan and 'capital deployment opportunities'.

sentences.text: The share repurchases are effected primarily through regular open-market purchases (which may include repurchase plans designed to comply with Rule 10b5-1 and accelerated share repurchases), the amounts and timing of which are determined primarily by our current and projected capital position, and capital deployment opportunities, but which may also be influenced by general market conditions and the prevailing price and trading volumes of our common stock.
The Board of Directors' authorization to repurchase common shares is utilized at management's discretion.
The $30 billion common share repurchase program approved by the Board of Directors does not establish specific price targets or timetables.

Management determines the amount and timing of common share repurchases based on various factors, including market conditions; legal and regulatory considerations affecting the amount and timing of repurchase activity; the Firm's capital position (taking into account goodwill and intangibles); organic capital generation; current and proposed future capital requirements; and other investment opportunities.

comparisons.peer_topic: Federal Reserve Capital Planning and Stress Test Requirements
comparisons.peer_summary: The company is subject to Federal Reserve capital planning and stress test requirements under the CCAR framework, requiring annual submission of a capital plan that includes a nine-quarter description of planned capital actions and maintenance of capital above minimum ratios, while its U.S. Bank Subsidiaries are exempt from company-run stress test requirements due to their asset size.
comparisons.comparison: GS and MS both identify the submission of an annual capital plan to the Federal Reserve as a key governance mechanism for share repurchases. GS details that this plan includes planned repurchases for each quarter. Similarly, MS states it must submit an annual capital plan to the Federal Reserve that includes a description of all planned capital actions, explicitly listing 'stock repurchases' as a capital distribution that must be included in the nine-quarter planning horizon.

sentences.text: On an annual basis, we submit a Board of Directors of Group Inc. (Board) approved capital plan to the Federal Reserve, which includes planned share repurchases for each quarter.

We must submit, on at least an annual basis, a capital plan to the Federal Reserve, taking into account the results of separate annual stress tests designed by us and the Federal Reserve, so that the Federal Reserve may assess our systems and processes that incorporate forward-looking projections of revenues and losses to monitor and maintain our internal capital adequacy.

The capital plan must include a description of all planned capital actions over a nine-quarter planning horizon, including any issuance or redemption of a debt or equity capital instrument, any capital distribution (i.e., payments of dividends or stock repurchases) and any similar action that the Federal Reserve determines could impact our consolidated capital.
